children.name: Cnemophilus
children.description: A genus of stout, medium-sized passerines endemic to the montane forests of New Guinea, superficially resembling birds-of-paradise but now placed in their own family. Males are brilliantly coloured in iridescent blues, purples, and yellows, while females are dull olive-brown. Their diet consists primarily of fruit, and they build domed nests in tree forks.

children.name: Cnemophilus loriae
children.description: Loria's satinbird or velvet satinbird (Cnemophilus loriae), formerly known as Loria's bird-of-paradise, is a species of bird in the family Cnemophilidae. It is found in the New Guinea Highlands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Cnemophilus macgregorii
children.description: The crested satinbird (Cnemophilus macgregorii), formerly known as the crested bird-of-paradise, is a species of bird in the satinbird family Cnemophilidae.

children.name: Loboparadisea
children.description: A monotypic genus of satinbird endemic to the mountains of New Guinea, with the male possessing a bizarre fleshy yellow wattle around the bill. The genus name meaning 'lobe-paradise bird' reflects its historical misclassification as a bird-of-paradise. It is a frugivore of the mid-montane forests.

children.name: Loboparadisea sericea
children.description: The yellow-breasted satinbird (Loboparadisea sericea), formerly known as the yellow-breasted bird-of-paradise and also known as the silken satinbird, is a species of bird in the family Cnemophilidae. It is monotypic within the genus Loboparadisea. It is found in the New Guinea highlands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.
